key_insight: Vision-Language-Action models frequently ignore language intent and exploit visual shortcuts from training data; this paper systematically exposes these "counterfactual failures" and proposes evaluation and mitigation strategies so VLAs act according to instructions rather than dataset biases.
problem_solved: Detects and reduces cases where VLAs repeat habitual visual behaviors or pick frequently seen objects regardless of language, i.e., failing to ground instructions when scene-specific supervision is weak.
method: Introduce a counterfactual evaluation protocol/benchmark that swaps objects/contexts and measures whether actions follow language intent or visual priors.
Define diagnostic metrics to quantify counterfactual failures and attribute errors to vision-dominant shortcuts.

Propose mitigation approaches (e.g., counterfactual data augmentation, reinforced language-conditioned supervision, and regularization to rebalance vision vs. language signals) to reduce shortcut-driven behavior.
impact: Provides practical tools and interventions so researchers and engineers can evaluate and improve instruction fidelity in VLAs, increasing reliability and safety for robotic and embodied-AI applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side example sequence: original instruction vs. counterfactual scene showing correct vs. shortcut-driven action

paper_title: When Vision Overrides Language: Evaluating and Mitigating Counterfactual Failures in VLAs
paper_authors: Yu Fang, Yuchun Feng, Dong Jing, Jiaqi Liu, Yue Yang
